verifications.note: TransCanada (TC Energy) press release, March 1, 2019: 'FERC has approved the full in-service of its Mountaineer XPress (MXP) project, allowing the company to increase the flow of gas on MXP and begin operating its Gulf XPress (GXP) project.' Uses the word 'operating' directly for GXP.

Reuters, Feb 2019: 'The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said on Monday it approved a request by TransCanada Corp's Columbia unit to put part of the company's $600 million Gulf XPress natural gas pipeline into service in Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (TC Energy's own release and Reuters wire coverage) confirm Gulf XPress reached in-service/operating status in Feb-Mar 2019, corroborating the recorded Status=operating. No indication in either source, or found elsewhere this pass, that the project was later idled or retired. BIC Magazine's article on the same event is a near-verbatim republish of the Reuters wire story ('The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said to Reuters it approved...') and is not counted as a second independent source, though it is consistent.

verifications.note: Reuters: '...put part of the company's $600 million Gulf XPress natural gas pipeline into service...'; also 'The 0.88-billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) Gulf XPress project...'
TC Energy: GXP facilities 'will provide additional capacity of [530] million cubic feet of natural gas per day on the Columbia Gulf Transmission System' -- a natural gas pipeline throughout.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both independent sources describe Gulf XPress uniformly as a natural gas pipeline/project on the Columbia Gulf Transmission System, matching the recorded Fuel=Gas.

verifications.note: TC Energy release dated 'HOUSTON, March 01, 2019': FERC 'allowing the company to increase the flow of gas on MXP and begin operating its Gulf XPress (GXP) project', and GXP 'is expected to be placed into full service in the coming weeks' -- i.e. partial-to-full in-service both fall in 2019.
Reuters article published Feb 2019 (byline timestamp 1549913141): FERC 'approved... to put part of... Gulf XPress natural gas pipeline into service'.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (Reuters, Feb 2019; TC Energy, Mar 1 2019) both place Gulf XPress's partial in-service, and imminent full in-service, in 2019, matching recorded StartYear1=2019. Neither source gives a specific month for full (as opposed to partial) in-service beyond 'the coming weeks' from March 1, 2019, so StartMonth1 is left unaddressed here (not in scope: brief's Start unit only carries StartYear1 in `values`).

verifications.note: Reuters: 'The 0.88-billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) Gulf XPress project includes construction of seven new compressor stations...' = 880 MMcf/d, within 0.6% of the recorded 875.00 MMcf/d.

TC Energy: the four compressor stations placed into partial service 'will provide additional capacity of [530] million cubic feet of natural gas per day on the Columbia Gulf Transmission System, which equates to approximately 60 percent of the project's total capacity' -- implying total capacity of ~530/0.60 = ~883 MMcf/d, within ~1% of the recorded 875.00.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Reuters states total project capacity directly as 0.88 bcfd (880 MMcf/d), within rounding of the recorded 875.00 MMcf/d. TC Energy's own release independently corroborates via its partial-capacity-as-percent-of-total statement (~883 MMcf/d implied), also within rounding. FLAG on the TC Energy page's raw text: it literally reads '530,000 million cubic feet of natural gas per day' (i.e. 530 Bcf/d), which is off by 1000x and is almost certainly a typo/formatting error in the source HTML for '530 million cubic feet per day' (0.53 Bcf/d) -- the intended figure is clear from context (530 MMcf/d = ~60% of an ~875-883 MMcf/d project, matching Reuters' 0.88 bcfd), so it was read as such rather than taken literally. No discrepancy material enough to warrant a validity flag on the recorded Capacity value itself.

verifications.note: Reuters: 'The 0.88-billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) Gulf XPress project includes construction of seven new compressor stations in Kentucky, Tennessee and Mississippi' -- describes the entire project as compressor-station construction, with no new pipeline mileage mentioned.

TC Energy: 'Partial in-service of the approximately US$600-million GXP project includes placing into service four new compressor stations located in Kentucky, Tennessee and Mississippi' -- again, compressor stations only, no new line pipe referenced anywhere in the release for GXP (as distinct from MXP, which the same release separately describes as new pipe + looping + compressor modifications).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both independent sources consistently describe Gulf XPress's entire physical scope as new/uprated compressor stations on the existing Columbia Gulf Transmission System, with zero mention of new pipeline segments or mileage anywhere in either release -- this is consistent with the recorded LengthKnown=0.00 km (a compression-capacity expansion, not new pipe). Marked medium rather than high because this is an inference from the absence of any pipe-construction language (a capacity project) rather than an explicit 'zero miles of new pipe' statement in either source; no source found this pass that states a nonzero length for GXP specifically, which would have contradicted the recorded value.

verifications.note: Reuters: 'Gulf XPress is one of several pipelines designed to connect growing output in the Marcellus and Utica shale basins in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio with customers in the U.S. Southeast and Gulf Coast' and '...seven new compressor stations in Kentucky, Tennessee and Mississippi' -- corroborates a West Virginia-region origin feeding a Mississippi/Gulf Coast terminus.

TC Energy: GXP compressor stations 'located in Kentucky, Tennessee and Mississippi' feeding 'the Columbia Gulf Transmission System' -- corroborates Mississippi as the system's southern end; page metadata tags the release with 'West Virginia' alongside GXP/MXP.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources corroborate the recorded EndState/Province=Mississippi (Columbia Gulf Transmission System terminus) and the general Appalachian-Basin-to-Gulf-Coast corridor consistent with a West Virginia start region. Neither source names 'Marshall County' specifically, or otherwise confirms the start point at the county level -- that finer-grained detail is NOT independently corroborated by what was opened this pass (a further web search for 'Gulf Xpress' + 'Marshall County' returned no usable result; this session's search-tool budget was exhausted, so only direct-URL/curl access was available). Recording as REFS_ADDED (partial, state/region-level corroboration for a location value with several sub-fields) rather than UNRESOLVED, since real corroborating evidence was found for most of the value -- but the Marshall County start-county detail specifically should be treated as still needing a source if a stricter per-subfield standard is wanted.

verifications.note: Reuters: '...approved a request by TransCanada Corp's Columbia unit to put part of the company's $600 million Gulf XPress natural gas pipeline into service...'

TC Energy's own release: 'TransCanada Corporation... today announced... begin operating its Gulf XPress (GXP) project'; project described throughout as TransCanada's. Published on tcenergy.com, the company's current site.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (company's own release plus Reuters wire coverage) confirm sole ownership by TransCanada Corporation / its Columbia unit, matching recorded Owner1=TC Energy at 100%. TransCanada Corporation renamed itself TC Energy Corporation in May 2019 (a well-documented, undisputed corporate rename, not an ownership change) -- both March-2019 sources predate the rename and so say 'TransCanada', the same single entity now named TC Energy; no separate ref is needed for the rename itself.
